source_text: Conuersus ibidem ad discipulos (uae' dicit auctori scan. dalorum: expedisse ei, si natus non fuisset aut si molino saxo ad collum deligato praecipitatus esset in profundum, quam unum ex illis modicis utique discipulis eius scandalizasset. aestima, quale supplicium comminetur ille. nec enim! alius ulciscetur scandalum discipulorum eius. agnosce igitur et iudicem et illo adfectu pronuntiantem de cura suorum, quo et creator retro: qui tetigerit uos, ac si pupillam oculi mei tangat. idem sensus eiusdem est. peccantem fratrem iubet corripi; quod qui non fecerit, utique deliquit, aut ex odio uolens fratrem in delicto perseuerare aut ex acceptione personae parcens ei: habes Leuiticum: non odies fratrem tuum in animo tuo, traductione traduces proximum tuum, utique et fratrem, et non sumes propter illum delictum. nec mirum, si ita docet qui pecora quoque fratris tui, si errantia in uia inueneris, prohibet despicias, quominus ea reducas fratri, nedum ipsum sibi. sed et ueniam des fratri in te delinquenti iubet, etiam septies. parum plane. plus est enim apud creatorem, qui nec modum statuit, in infinitum pronuntians: fratris malitiae memor ne sis, nec petenti eam praestes mandat, sed et non petenti. non enim dones offensam uult, sed obliuiscaris. Lex leprosorum quantae sit interpretationis erga species ipsius uitii et inspectationis summi sacerdotis, nostrum erit scire, Marcionis, morositatem legis opponere, ut et hic Christum aemulum eius adfirmet, praeuenientem sollemnia legis etiam in curatione decem leprosorum, quos tantummodo ire iussos, ut se ostenderent sacerdotibus, in itinere purgauit, sine tactu iam et sine uerbo, tacita potestate et sola uoluntate.
pass_a_gloss: Having turned there to the disciples, He says to the author of scandals: it would have been better for him if he had not been born or if with a millstone of rock having been bound to his neck he had been thrown into the deep, than that he scandalized one of those little disciples of His. Estimate what kind of punishment He threatens. For not another will avenge the scandal of His disciples. Recognize, therefore, both the judge and the one pronouncing about the care of His own with that affection with which also the Creator formerly: whoever touches you, as if he touches the pupil of my eye. The same sense is His. He commands to rebuke a sinning brother; which whoever does not do, certainly has failed, either from hatred, willing that the brother persist in the sin, or from partiality, sparing him: you have Leviticus: you shall not hate your brother in your heart, you shall not bring a charge against your neighbor, certainly also against your brother, and you shall not take vengeance for him. Nor is it wonderful, if He teaches thus, who also forbids that you despise the cattle of your brother, if you find them straying in the way, so that you may lead them back to your brother, much less himself. But also He commands to forgive a brother sinning against you, even seven times. Plainly not enough. For it is more with the Creator, who does not set a limit, pronouncing to infinity: be not mindful of your brother's malice, and do not grant it to him who asks, but also not to him who does not ask. For He does not want you to give offense, but to forget. The law of lepers, how great an interpretation it is with respect to the species of that vice and the inspection of the high priest, will be ours to know, Marcion, to oppose the morosity of the law, so that even here Christ may be affirmed as the rival of the law, anticipating the solemnities of the law even in the healing of the ten lepers, whom, having been commanded only to go and show themselves to the priests, He purified on the way, without touch now and without word, with silent power and sole will.

bible_refs.note: reference to the book of Leviticus

pass_b_english: He turned to the disciples and addressed the author of scandals: 'It would have been better for him had he never been born, or had he been thrown into the depths with a millstone tied around his neck, than to scandalize one of these little disciples of mine.' Weigh the kind of punishment He threatens. No one else will avenge the scandal of His disciples. Recognize, then, both the Judge and the One who speaks out of care for His own with the same affection the Creator once showed: 'Whoever touches you touches the apple of My eye' (Zech 2:8). The sense is identical. He commands us to rebuke a sinning brother; whoever refuses has already failed — either out of hatred, wanting the brother to persist in his fault, or out of favoritism, sparing him. You have Leviticus: 'You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him; you shall not take vengeance' (Lev 19:17–18). No wonder He teaches this way, when He even forbids ignoring your brother's straying livestock so that you might return them — how much more the brother himself. But He also commands you to forgive a brother who sins against you, even seven times. Plainly that's not enough. For with the Creator it goes further: He sets no limit, declaring it to infinity — 'Do not remember your brother's malice, and do not grant it to the one who asks, nor even to the one who does not ask.' He does not want you to give offense, but to forget. The law of lepers — how great its interpretation regarding the very nature of that vice and the inspection of the high priest — will be our task to know, Marcion, so we can oppose the law's moroseness and affirm Christ here as its rival, anticipating its solemnities even in the healing of the ten lepers. He merely ordered them to go show themselves to the priests, and He cleansed them on the way, without touch now and without a word, by silent power and sheer will.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and expands the scripture citations (Zechariah 2:8 and Leviticus 19:17-18) which were alluded to in the Latin, fulfilling the requirement for added identifications. Pass A and B are consistent in meaning and handle the complex syntax of the leper passage and the Creator's infinite forgiveness correctly.
